newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sugar beet said doing well despite rain.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sugar beet said doing well despite rain.

text.p: Ukrainian sugar beets are developing well despite recent heavy rains throughout the country, with the final crop expected the same or better than last year's 24 million tonnes, a senior industry official said on Monday.
"Sugar beets are growing better than last year, so the crop may equal last year's or maybe turn out to be a little better," Leonid Bershtein, deputy director of the Sugar Research Institute, said.
He said there could be a larger crop even though Ukraine planted only one million hectares to sugar beet against 1.2 million ha in 1996.
But recent rains had spurred weed growth and some beet damage had been reported due to rain and hail.
"People and the technology we have can't keep up in the fight against the weeds," Bershtein said.
Economy Ministry officials said earlier this month Ukraine expected a sugar beet crop of 30-31 million tonnes.
Petro Pasichnyk, a technical analyst at the Agriculture Ministry, said testing of beets for sugar content would begin on August 1, since recent rains had prevented accurate readings.
"Right now, the beet roots weigh about 70 to 80 grams. We will test when they are 100 grams," Pasichnyk said.
